P-Card Use: Quick Guide

From the ORA eTraining module "Purchasing with Purpose: Procurement on Sponsored Projects" (lesson 11 of 15).
Procurements With The MSU P-Card
This section of the module provides a quick reference for key MSU Purchasing Card ( information that may be relevant to research administration and sponsored project purchases at Morgan State University. This lesson is not a substitute for formal P-Card training; employees must complete required training through the MSU P-Card Office before receiving or using a University P-Card.

How To: Request a MSU P-Card
P-Card Application Process
The P-Card Office administers the process of providing purchasing cards to authorized users. Please review the steps and associated documents outlined here to reduce errors/delays in processing your request.
Summary

Speak With Your Supervisor
Before requesting a purchasing card please speak to your immediate supervisor. It is best practice to determine how many individuals under your project require a purchasing card, which budgets should be included in the request, and who your authorized approver will be.
Email the MSU P-Card Office
Your supervisor will need to send a formal request for your card via email to the P-Card Office (pcard@morgan.edu). Mrs. Ransom, or a member of her team, will review your request and begin next steps.
P-Card Office Provides Documentation
The P-Card Office will verify your eligibility to receive a card. If approved, their office will send a cardholder agreement, purchasing card application form, and the P-Card user manual for you to complete/review and return.
P-Card Office Sends Documents
The P-Card Office will review the documents before processing them through US Bank and the State of Maryland. Additionally, they will provide P-card orientation materials to the cardholder.
US Bank Sends Card to Bear Card Office
US Bank will process the card request and generate a card in the cardholder's name to be sent to the Bear Card Office.
Cardholder Arranges for Card Pickup
Upon the card's arrival on campus, the P-Card Office will contact the cardholder to arrange a pickup time for the card. After pickup, the cardholder will call US Bank to activate the card. It is then ready for use! BEARcard Center Location : Tyler Hall, Room 306 Contact : x4045, bearcard@morgan.edu Please schedule a time to pick up your P-Card using the link below: Schedule a Time
P-Card Reconciliation: Supporting Documents
Supporting documentation is required for proper p-card use and timely reconciliation. Cardholders should collect and organize receipts, invoices, business purpose details, and other required documentation as purchases occur, rather than waiting until the monthly submission deadline.

You can access your card statement online at access.usbank.com after creating an account. Use the Organization Short Name of "MD". Below is a pdf instruction manual outlining account access procedures.
US Bank Statement
Ensure invoices meet the detail requirement outlined in the Processing Invoices for Payment lesson of this module.
Transaction Invoices
It is best practice to complete the log as you spend on a project. No need to wait until the submission deadline to complete your log, collect invoices, and ensure signatures are present as requested.

FAAINVT: P-Card Reconciliation
Banner P-Card Transaction Reconciliation
P-card transactions must be reconciled in Banner by the required monthly submission deadline, which is currently the 8th of the month . Timely reconciliation helps ensure charges are reviewed, properly documented, and assigned to the correct funding source before the accounting period closes.
Banner Links Landing Page
Start by navigating to the "Banner Links" landing page, select "Native Banner", and enter your MSU login credentials.
FAAINVT
Enter "Purchase Card Transaction Maintenance" or "FAAINVT" in the search bar and select the page from the dropdown menu.
Cardholder Details
In the Cardholder ID cell, enter your MSU ID #. In the Type cell, ensure "Not Fed Transactions" is selected. Click the Go button in the top right corner.
Transaction Selection
Here you will find each transaction for the active reconciliation period. A description of the currently selected transaction will be provided under the "Vendor Description" section which details the vendor, transaction date, and total cost of the expense. At the bottom of the screen there is a count of of total transactions for the period. You will use the arrows here to select the transaction you need to update the funding/accounting for. Start with your first transaction (1 of X) and use the "Next Section" button (right button of the two) at the bottom left corner of the screen to move onto the accounting/finance section for that transaction.
Accounting Information
Using the right "Next Section" button, work your way down to the Details section of this page. There, enter the appropriate index and Banner account code for the identified transaction. Once entered, click the "Save" button at the bottom right of the screen. Use the right "Next Section" button to return to the previous Vendor Information page. Using the arrows at the bottom left corner of the screen select the next transaction (2 of X) and repeat this step to enter the appropriate accounting information and save your updates. Repeat this process until all transactions have updated accounting information.
Please Note: Transactions not allocated to the appropriate account/index by the monthly reconciliation deadline will, by default, be allocated to the cardholder's default index noted in FAAINVT's "Default Accounting Distribution". All charges will be assigned to account code 09950.

DocuSign: P-Card Transaction Log
State Transaction Log
Submitting your completed State of Maryland Transaction Log for review is the final step of your monthly p-card reconciliation duties. The MSU P-Card Office will review your documents for accuracy and reach out for any additionally required information.
Enter Transactions As They Occur
It is best practice to enter transactions on your log as they occur. This helps to ensure your Banner reconciliation goes smoothly and reduces the risk of being unable to complete the log in a time for the monthly submission deadline (15th of the month).
Data Entry Part 1
Above we see the top of the State of Maryland Transaction Log sheet. Here, you must enter the following information: Cardholder Name Month/Year Department Primary Index If unknown, this can be found on your Banner P-Card Reconciliation page (aka FAAINVT) Last six digits of your card number
Transaction Details Part 1
The transaction details portion of the log has 7 columns to complete for each transaction. Starting from the left: Order Date This should match the "Transaction Date" for the purchase on your US Bank Statement. Vendor Name Purchase/Refund Amount A refund amount will be entered with a minus (-) sign in front of the dollar cost. Also, please contact the vendor to receive some form of confirmation of the refund amount (invoice/receipt, email, etc.)
Transaction Details Part 2
Sales Tax (if any) Sales tax charges should not be assessed on purchases using your State of Maryland purchasing card. If you are charged sales tax it is your responsibility to work with the vendor to have the tax charge remitted to your card. Exceptions to this rule include hotel/lodging and flight/train travel expenses. Description of Purchase The description does not need to be highly detailed (product specs, serial number, etc), but should be detailed enough to clearly describe the item/service rendered. If the cost is travel-related, you must note the traveler name and the associated travel authorization number in this line as well. Index/Budget Here you enter the six-digit index code assigned to the project/budget funding the transaction. This information, along with the account information, should match your entries during your Banner reconciliation on the 8th of the month. Account The correct account code to enter here will be based on the type of transaction. A list of Banner account codes is included in this module for your reference. If you are unsure which account code to assign you should reach out to your departmental budget officer or directly to pcardreconciliation@morgan.edu.
Verify Log Accuracy
At the end of the month you should review your US Bank Statement and verify that all monthly charges are accurately noted in your transaction log. Check the "Statement Total" on your US Bank statement and ensure it matches your "Log Total" on the State of Maryland Transaction Log.
Upload Documents to DocuSign
Utilizing the DocuSign link here , you will upload your US Bank Statement, State of Maryland Transaction Log, and all associated invoices into a DocuSign envelope. Invoices should be in order according to the order date on your transaction log. You will need your bank statement and transaction log signed by the following individuals: Cardholder: This is the person named on the p-card. Authorized Approver: This is the person who is responsible for verifying that all p-card charges are allowable and allocable to the noted budget. PCPA Review: This will be the P-Card Office staff member that reviews your log and associated documentation. You will want to use the email address pcardreconciliation@morgan.edu for this approval.

Additional P-Card Considerations
https://articulateusercontent.com/assets/rise/assets/block-defaults/paraglide_thumb.jpg
Split Purchasing
Split Purchasing refers to the act of dividing a single transaction into several smaller transactions in order to circumvent increased Procurement oversight. Instead of splitting the purchase, the faculty/staff member must go through the Procurement process via requisition/purchase order. Repeated offenses will result in card termination. Example : You receive a quote for lab supplies that totals $6,000. In order to bypass the $5,000 purchase limit restriction, you ask the vendor to provide two quotes for $3,000 each in order to process payment with your card.
Charge Denial reasons
Maximum Purchase Limit Met: Your purchasing card has a single purchase limit referenced in your P-Card Office documentation. Any expense greater than that would need to either be sourced from multiple vendors or go through the procurement process via requisition/purchase order. Additionally, your card has a monthly purchasing limit set by the P-Card Office on a case-by-case basis. This amount can range up to $50,000 per month. Any threshold greater than $50,000 would require approval from the State of Maryland General Accounting Division (GAD). Fraud Protection: US Bank maintains certain protocols to help reduce the incidents of fraudulent p-card purchases. For example, if you haven't used your card for an extended period of time, then attempt to make a large purchase, US Bank may stop payment processing. In this case, you can call US BANK customer service at the number on your purchasing card to ask that the stop payment be lifted. MCC Group Block: The State and University prohibit certain Merchant Category Code (MCC) groups from purchasing card use. The Morgan State P-Card Office does not have the authority to override state blocks on MCC groups. For example, Orbitz.com is coded as an airline site (airline tickets being a banned card expense) and may not be an available travel resource.
